content:
Today, Instapaper released the 10th version of its iPhone and iPad apps, bringing a number of improvements alongside a major redesign of its web platform. Here are the details.

"The biggest update to the iOS app in over a decade"

Instapaper today (via MacMagazine) announced updates to its iOS app, added new AI voice features to its Android app, and gave its website an overhaul.

Instapaper for iOS version 10 adds support for Liquid Glass and introduces four reading fonts:

Literata: a serif font designed by Google for Google Play Books. New York: a serif font designed by Apple for iOS. Open Sans: a sans-serif font commissioned by Google. Atkinson Hyperlegible: a sans-serif font developed by the Braille Institute.

This update also adds a Home Screen widget, which Instapaper says displays your current article and recently saved items, while also serving as a one-tap shortcut to start reading.

For iPad users, Instapaper says this update improves multitasking, while both iPhone and iPad users will notice more reliable background syncing, faster article download times, and a redesigned onboarding tour.

Instapaper says today's update is the biggest in over a decade and also includes:

Folder Counts: All folders now display the number of articles or notes they contain. If you find folder counts more anxiety-inducing instead, you can turn them off in Settings > Behavior > Folder Counts. Folder Sorting: Want to sort your folders or tags? Tap the "…" menu next to the folder title, then choose your preferred sort order. Article List Appearance: We've added a compact mode, new typography and styles, and an easy way to customize the look of your article list. In the article list, tap "…" and then tap "Appearance" to adjust the style, font, and image thumbnails.

Finally, Instapaper overhauled its web platform with a three-column reader and keyboard shortcuts, while the Android app now also supports AI voice features.
